newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate passes budget measure, goes to Clinton.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate passes budget measure, goes to Clinton.

text.p: The U.S. Senate on Thursday approved bipartisan legislation designed to balance the budget by 2002 and shrink the size of government, sending the measure to President Bill Clinton for his promised signature.

With both Democrats and Republicans declaring victory, the Senate approved the measure by a vote of 85-15 and prepared to open debate on a companion measure cutting taxes by a net $95 billion over five years.

"On both sides of the aisle and both ends of Pennsylvania Avenue, Republicans and Democrats, House and Senate and, yes, the president are all saying, 'This is good for America'," Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott said.
Twelve of the chamber's 55 Republicans voted against the measure along with three of its 45 Democrats.
The legislation makes spending cuts needed to implement a five-year balanced budget deal between Congress and the White House.

The measure approved by the Senate reducess spending on mandatory programmes such as Medicare and Medicaid by about $130 billion over five years, creates a new children's health programme and restores cuts made in a welfare law last year.
It also calls on Congress to find another $140 billion in reductions over that same period as part of annual spending bills, but does not specify where they should come from.
